lesson.title: Per cent means out of 100
lesson.body: 45% means 45 out of 100: 45/100 = 9/20 = 0.45. The same amount written three ways.

lesson.title: Moving between forms
lesson.body: Per cent to decimal: divide by 100. Decimal to per cent: multiply by 100. Fraction to per cent: make the bottom 100.

lesson.title: Per cent of a number
lesson.body: 25% of 80 is 25/100 × 80 = 20. Or use friendly per cents: 10% of 80 is 8, so 25% is 8 + 8 + 4 = 20.

lesson.title: Finding the whole
lesson.body: If 20% of a number is 12, then 10% is 6 and 100% is 60.

lesson.title: Discounts
lesson.body: A ₱400 bag at 25% off: the discount is 25% of ₱400 = ₱100, so you pay ₱400 − ₱100 = ₱300.

lesson.title: Increases and interest
lesson.body: 10% more than 300 is 300 + 30 = 330. ₱1000 kept for a year at 5% interest earns ₱50.

templates.construct: Write a per cent as a fraction in lowest terms

formats.prompt: Write {p}% as a fraction in lowest terms.

hints: Simplify {p}/100: divide the top and bottom by {g}.

distractors.feedback: {frac(value)} is {p} tenths. Per cent means out of 100: {p}/100.
{frac(value)} is 100/{p}, upside down. {p}% is {p}/100.

templates.construct: Write a per cent as a decimal

formats.prompt: Write {p}% as a decimal.

hints: Per cent means hundredths: divide by 100.
Dividing by 100 moves the decimal point two places to the left.
Start from {p} and move the point two places left.
steps: Move the point two places left

distractors.feedback: {value} moves the point one place. Per cent means hundredths: move it two places.
{value} is the per cent number. As a decimal, divide by 100.
{value} moves the point three places. Divide by 100: two places.

templates.construct: Write a fraction as a per cent by making the denominator 100

formats.prompt: Write {frac(a / b)} as a per cent.

hints: 100 ÷ {b} = {100 / b}, so multiply the top and the bottom by {100 / b}.

distractors.feedback: {value}% is just the top number. Make the bottom 100 first.
{value}% makes the fraction out of 10. Per cent is out of 100.

templates.construct: Write a decimal as a per cent

formats.prompt: Write {d} as a per cent.

hints: To make a per cent, multiply by 100.
Multiplying by 100 moves the point two places to the right.
{d} with the point two places right = ?
steps: Move the point two places right

distractors.feedback: {value}% moves the point one place. Multiply by 100: two places.
{value}% is the decimal as it was. Multiply by 100 to make a per cent.

templates.construct: Find a per cent of a whole number

formats.prompt: What is {p}% of {n}?
There are {n} pupils in a school, and {p}% of them walk to school. How many walk to school?

distractors.feedback: {value} is {n} × {p}. Per cent means out of 100: divide by 100.
{value} is what is left after {p}%. The question asks for the {p}% itself.
{value} divides by 10. Per cent means out of 100.

templates.construct: Write one number as a per cent of another

formats.prompt: {a} out of {n} pupils wear glasses. What per cent of the pupils wear glasses?
Ana got {a} out of {n} on a test. What is her score as a per cent?

hints: Write it as a fraction, then make the bottom 100.

distractors.feedback: {value}% is the count. Write {a} out of {n} as out of 100.
{value} is the number who do not. The question asks about the {a}.

templates.construct: Find the whole from a per cent and its part

formats.prompt: {p}% of a number is {part}. What is the number?
Mila saves {p}% of her allowance. She saves ₱{part}. How much is her allowance?

hints: {part} is {p}% of the whole. Find 1% or 10% first.

distractors.feedback: {value} takes {p}% of {part}. Here {part} is the {p}%; find the whole.
{value} adds {p} to {part}. {part} is {p}% of the whole: find 100%.

formats.prompt: A bag costs ₱{price}. It is on sale at {p}% off. How much is the discount?
Shoes priced at ₱{price} are {p}% off. How many pesos are taken off?

hints: The discount is {p}% of the price.

distractors.feedback: ₱{value} is the sale price. The question asks for the discount.
{value} is the per cent, not the pesos. {p}% of ₱{price} is ₱{price} × {p} ÷ 100.

templates.construct: Find a sale price after a discount

formats.prompt: A bag costs ₱{price}. It is on sale at {p}% off. How much do you pay?
A shirt is priced at ₱{price}, with a {p}% discount. What is the sale price?

distractors.feedback: ₱{value} is the discount. Take it away from ₱{price}.
₱{value} takes off {p} pesos. {p}% of ₱{price} is ₱{off}.

templates.construct: Increase a number by a per cent

formats.prompt: A school had {n} pupils last year. This year it has {p}% more. How many pupils does it have now?
A farm picked {n} kg of mangoes last year and {p}% more this year. How many kilograms did it pick this year?

hints: Find {p}% of {n}, then add it on.

distractors.feedback: {value} is the increase. Add it to {n}.
{value} adds {p}. {p}% of {n} is {more}.

templates.construct: Find simple interest for one year

formats.prompt: ₱{P} is kept in a bank for one year at {r}% interest a year. How much interest does it earn?
A cooperative pays {r}% interest a year. How much interest does ₱{P} earn in one year?

hints: The interest for one year is {r}% of ₱{P}.

distractors.feedback: ₱{value} is the money plus the interest. The question asks for the interest.
₱{value} is ₱{P} × {r}. Per cent means out of 100: divide by 100.

templates.construct: Find a discount, ignoring the money the buyer has

formats.prompt: A pair of shoes costs ₱{p}, and the store gives {d}% off. There is ₱{w} in Mia's wallet. How much is the discount?

hints: The question asks for the discount, not what is paid.
The ₱{w} in the wallet is not needed.
templates.explain: {d}% of ₱{p} = ₱{answer}. The money in the wallet was extra information.

distractors.feedback: ₱{value} is the sale price. The question asks for the discount: {d}% of ₱{p}.
₱{value} is the change from ₱{w}. The question asks only for the discount.

templates.construct: Compare two discounted prices to find the better deal

formats.prompt: Store A sells a school bag for ₱{p1} at {d1}% off. Store B sells the same bag for ₱{p2} at {d2}% off. How much less do you pay at the store with the better deal?

hints: Find what you pay at each store, after its discount.
Store A: {d1}% of ₱{p1} is ₱{p1 * d1 / 100}. Store B: {d2}% of ₱{p2} is ₱{p2 * d2 / 100}.
Take each discount off, then find the difference.
templates.explain: You pay ₱{s1} at Store A and ₱{s2} at Store B, so the better deal is ₱{answer} less.

distractors.feedback: ₱{value} is the difference between the two discounts. Compare what you pay: ₱{s1} and ₱{s2}.
₱{value} is the difference before the discounts. Take each discount off first: ₱{s1} and ₱{s2}.

templates.construct: Find a percent increase from the old and new prices

formats.prompt: The price of a school bag went up from ₱{a} to ₱{b}. By what percent did it go up?
A family's monthly water bill went up from ₱{a} to ₱{b}. By what percent did it go up?

hints: First find how much it went up.
₱{b - a} out of the old amount, ₱{a}, as a percent.
steps: Compare it with the old amount: {b - a}/{a}
templates.explain: It went up by ₱{b - a} on ₱{a}, which is {answer}%.

distractors.feedback: {value}% is the increase in pesos, ₱{b - a}. As a percent of the old amount: ₱{b - a} ÷ ₱{a} × 100.
{fmt(value)}% compares the increase with the new amount, ₱{b}. Compare it with the old amount, ₱{a}.

templates.construct: Find how many are left in a group after two parts given in per cent

formats.prompt: Of the {total} pupils in a class, {p1}% walk to school and {p2}% ride a jeepney. The rest come by tricycle. How many come by tricycle?
A farmer plants {total} seedlings: {p1}% are tomatoes and {p2}% are eggplants. The rest are peppers. How many are peppers?

hints: First find the per cent left: 100% − {p1}% − {p2}%.

distractors.feedback: {value} is the per cent left, {value}%. Now find {value}% of {total}.
{value} is {p1}% of {total}. The question asks about the rest.
{value} takes {p1} and {p2} from {total} as if they were counts. They are per cents: find {r}% of {total}.
